answer: Whether agents trade crystal, map karst, or insure basalt shipments, a marketplace can require each bidding identity to lock a refundable bond. If an identity wins a contract but fails to deliver by a verifiable deadline, the bond is forfeited. An attacker flooding auctions with fake bidders must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing bonds on undelivered contracts. This raises the cost of disruption without preventing a wealthy attacker from participating.
